title: SPA fallback condition is always-true, making the final 404 branch unreachable
detail: api/routes.ts trailing 404 guards on `!startsWith('/api/')` but /api/ returns earlier (line 39-41), so `!pathname.startsWith("/api/")` is always true at the catch-all (line 67) and the `return new Response("Not found", {status:404})` (line 71) is unreachable dead code. This is a correctness/quality cleanup, NOT an exploitable security issue. Re-reported 12 runs, never fixed. This run (2026-06-20T07-55) re-confirmed and clarified: simplify the guard to a bare final `return serveFile(index.html)` with the 404 dropped.

title: Path-prefix containment checks omit the trailing separator (path traversal)
detail: `startsWith(resolvedDir)` must append `path.sep` or siblings like `outputs-evil` bypass it. Recurs across gallery/caption/upload/config variants over 7 runs. This run (2026-06-19T22:47) re-flagged it at critical severity in api/config.ts validatePythonPath: `resolved.startsWith(REPO_DIR)` (no trailing sep, so `<REPO_DIR>-evil`/`<REPO_DIR>-extra` siblings match) COMBINED with `resolved.includes('/.venv/')` substring (any path containing that string passes). A sibling-repo binary like `<REPO_DIR>-evil/.venv/bin/python` satisfies BOTH checks, then handleVerifyPython Bun.spawnSync([bin,'-c','import mlx...']) executes it — RCE from a client-controlled config value.

title: handleVerifyPython forwards raw err.message / Python stderr to the client
detail: api/config.ts returns the spawn exception message AND the last stderr line to the client (path/env disclosure). Both paths need fixing: catch block returns e.message; non-zero exit path exposes Python traceback last line. Log server-side, return generic. Re-flagged 13 runs.

title: killJob lacks a pid guard and finalizes before stream drain (both the immediate-sync path AND the 5s SIGTERM fallback)
detail: lib/subprocess.ts: guard `job.pid` before process.kill(); rely on proc.exited to finalize after streams drain rather than calling finalize() directly from killJob. The spawn path (lines 230-241) deliberately awaits Promise.all([stdoutDone, stderrDone]) before finalize so trailing log lines and Saved:/Manifest: markers persist. killJob's 5s SIGTERM fallback (lines 270-282) calls finalize('failed',-1) SYNCHRONOUS inside setTimeout WITHOUT awaiting the stream drains; once finalized=true, the proc.exited->drain->finalize path is a no-op, so a run.py child that takes the SIGTERM but flushes final output between 5s and actual exit drops those lines and any final 'Saved:' output paths. This run (2026-06-19T22:47) re-confirmed the 5s fallback reintroduces exactly the drain-before-finalize bug the comment at 262-269 warns about. Re-flagged 7 runs.

title: isPathAllowed() defaults to full REPO_DIR instead of narrow output dirs
detail: caption/upload/caption-GET accept arbitrary client paths but allow-scope is REPO_DIR, not OUTPUT_DIRS. Narrow to the minimum dir set (OUTPUT_DIRS + UPLOAD_DIR). The trailing-separator fix is already in place (line 38 uses d + path.sep), but the SCOPE is still the full repo. This run (2026-06-19T22:47) re-flagged api/caption.ts handleCaptionGet: it checks only isPathAllowed(imagePath) with the default allowedDirs=[...OUTPUT_DIRS, REPO_DIR], so a client can read ANY <anything>.caption.json under the entire repository; unlike handleCaptionRun, the GET path has no leading-dash guard and no output-dir containment. Re-flagged 7 runs.

title: clearJobs accepts arbitrary status without an allowlist (HTTP handler AND low-level manager)
detail: api/jobs.ts handleClearJobs casts `status` unchecked AND lib/subprocess.ts clearJobs(statuses) deletes matching jobs without restricting to CLEARABLE=['completed','failed']. Only the HTTP handler enforces the allowlist; any future internal caller (admin route, workflow script) invoking subprocessManager.clearJobs directly could pass ['running'] and silently kill+purge in-flight jobs (deleteJob also SIGTERMs running children). Validation must live at the trust boundary (the manager), not just the route. Clamp statuses inside clearJobs itself: filter to CLEARABLE before iterating. Re-flagged 4 runs.

title: FTS5 'optimize' runs after _indexed=true, so a thrown optimize masks build failure
detail: lib/gallery-index.ts buildIndex sets `_indexed = true` (line 50) BEFORE running `INSERT INTO images_fts(images_fts) VALUES('optimize')` (line 51). If optimize throws (corrupt/large FTS5 index, OOM), the exception propagates but isIndexed() already returns true, so handleGallerySearch never retries the build — subsequent searches run against a half-built/under-optimized index and return empty/wrong results with no rebuild triggered. Wrap DELETE+insertAll+optimize in try/catch; set _indexed=true ONLY after full success, reset to false on failure. Re-flagged 4 runs.

title: handlePutConfig accepts arbitrary outputDir/modelsDir without path-containment validation
detail: api/config.ts write-time path is not bounded — a client can point generation at any directory. Validate against an allowlist at write time; reject absolute paths or traversal (..) that escape the allowed root. At minimum require they resolve within REPO_DIR or its sibling output store. title: CSRF/origin check compares against the request's own Host header (DNS-rebinding bypass)
detail: api/routes.ts (line 94) and api/ws.ts (line 23): origin allowlist is derived from Host header — DNS-rebinding makes attacker origin match. Because no POST endpoint has other auth, a matching origin lets a malicious page POST /api/run, /api/upload, /api/config (combined with validatePythonPath = RCE), /api/gallery DELETE. Use a fixed allowlist: `new Set(['http://localhost:3099', 'http://127.0.0.1:3099'])`. Mirror in both HTTP routes and WS upgrade. This run (2026-06-20T04-15) re-flagged the same allowlist construction duplicated verbatim in routes.ts:95-116 and ws.ts:23-40 — the Host-derived port extraction + [127.0.0.1,localhost,[::1]] list is copy-pasted, and the default port '3099' is hardcoded as a string fallback in both (plus server.ts:15 numeric). Re-flagged 6 runs. NOTE (2026-06-20T23-13): csrf-rebinding-false-positive-loopback argues the cross-site bypass is a false positive (Origin/Host are browser-forbidden headers), so the security framing here is partly contested — but the DRY-duplication + fixed-allowlist hygiene recommendation stands. UPDATE (2026-06-21T03-54): the DRY-duplication was FIXED this run — the allowlist was extracted to lib/origin.ts originAllowed(origin,host) and both routes.ts + ws.ts now call it (see extract-shared-helper-eliminates-duplication-class). The Host-derived-port security concern is now consolidated behind one helper.

detail: api/gallery.ts + api/upload.ts: extension-only upload check + missing nosniff lets a polyglot payload execute. Sniff content and set headers. Retired: single-occurrence; the header/nosniff gap is already covered by missing-security-headers which recurs 5x at higher confidence.

detail: api/upload.ts: check Content-Length before req.formData() to fail-fast; post-parse check must remain as backstop (Content-Length can be spoofed). Re-flagged 3 runs.

title: job_failed WS message received but frontend never calls setOutputFiles for it
detail: frontend/hooks/ui/useWebSocket.ts: job_complete handler calls setOutputFiles but job_failed does not. The WS broadcast in api/ws.ts sends outputFiles for BOTH completed and failed jobs, so a job that fails mid-run carries already-produced outputs that the frontend silently discards. Fix: add `if (msg.outputFiles?.length) setOutputFiles(msg.outputFiles)` in the job_failed branch. Re-flagged 3 runs.

title: useCommandView substitutes WS logs over restored job logs even when job is not running
detail: frontend/hooks/commands/useCommandView.ts derivedJob uses WS `logs` when `logs.length > 0`, regardless of job.status. A restored completed/failed job can show stale WS logs from a prior subscription until subscribe() fires. Fix: gate the WS log substitution on `job.status === 'running' && logs.length > 0`. Re-flagged 3 runs.

title: WebSocket reconnect timer not cleared before setting new timer on close (double-reconnect) — bug recurs in the SHARED wsClient singleton after the useWebSocket fix
detail: The fix landed in frontend/hooks/ui/useWebSocket.ts:55 (`if (reconnectTimer.current) clearTimeout(reconnectTimer.current)`) but was NEVER PORTED to the shared broadcast singleton frontend/hooks/ui/wsClient.ts. This run (2026-06-20T04-15) re-flagged wsClient.ts:27 — ws.onclose assigns `_reconnectTimer = window.setTimeout(_connect, _reconnectDelay)` without first clearing a pending timer. If onclose fires twice in quick succession (ws.close() from onerror racing a transport close) the first handle is orphaned and both fire _connect. The singleton drives ALL broadcast listeners (useJobs revalidation, gallery-updated, hmr-reload), so a leaked timer storm degrades the whole SPA. Fix (same as the useWebSocket fix): `if (_reconnectTimer) clearTimeout(_reconnectTimer)` before the setTimeout. LESSON: a correctness fix applied to one site of a duplicated pattern must be grep-ported to every sibling site, or the bug class recurs. Re-flagged 4 runs.

title: Gallery DELETE companion-file cleanup uses only the verbatim base name, missing multi-segment suffixes (read/write asymmetry)
detail: api/gallery.ts handleGalleryDelete deletes `{base}.manifest.json` etc., but for relay/segment filenames like `output_20260611_193630_seg01.png` the real manifest is the parent stem `output_20260611_193630.manifest.json` (found by findCompanionJson via progressive suffix-stripping). The delete handler never strips these suffixes so orphaned .manifest.json/.run.json/.caption.json remain across output dirs. This run (2026-06-20T04-15) re-confirmed the exact asymmetry: READ path resolves companions by progressively stripping `_relay`/`_segXX`; DELETE path only strips the file extension. Fix: reuse findCompanionJson(dir, base, suffix) per companion type, then tryDelete the resolved path (export it; keeps delete symmetric with list). Re-flagged 4 runs.

title: validatePythonPath uses substring match for /.venv/ allowing arbitrary paths that contain the string
detail: api/config.ts `resolved.includes('/.venv/')` passes `/tmp/evil/.venv/bin/python` and `resolved.includes('/venv/')` passes `/home/attacker/venv/bin/malicious`. The malicious binary is then invoked by handleVerifyPython (Bun.spawnSync) and by caption/model-check via resolvePythonBin — an arbitrary-command-execution primitive via the config write endpoint. This run (2026-06-19T22:47) re-flagged it as severity:critical (the highest-severity finding). A sibling-repo binary like `<REPO_DIR>-evil/.venv/bin/python` passes BOTH the startsWith(REPO_DIR) check (prefix, no trailing sep) AND the includes('/.venv/') check. Since a config PUT writes it to disk, every subsequent run.py/check-model/caption spawn runs arbitrary code as the server user. Fix: drop the includes() branches entirely; use strict directory containment with a trailing separator — `if (!resolved.startsWith(REPO_DIR + path.sep)) return false;`. If an out-of-repo venv must be supported, validate against an explicit allowlist of resolved venv roots. Re-flagged 5 runs. Re-flagged this run (2026-06-23T22-35) as correctness-config.ts-25 (downgraded to low/info): this run noted the companion nuance that path.resolve does NOT resolve symlinks (use fs.realpathSync for full hardening), but on a localhost single-operator server venv symlinks are deliberately allowed — threat model treats the operator as the only attacker with a shell. The includes() substring + startsWith(no-sep) RCE class is still the live concern; the symlink-resolve gap is defense-in-depth only.

title: callDeepSeek makes outbound fetch without an AbortSignal timeout (indefinite hang, request-slot exhaustion)
detail: lib/knowledge-extractor.ts callDeepSeek: no AbortSignal on the fetch to api.deepseek.com. A slow/stalled response holds the server request open indefinitely, exhausting request slots on the single Bun event loop. The function is awaited end-to-end through the HTTP handler so the client connection also hangs. Compare with vlm.ts which uses AbortSignal.timeout(5000). Fix: add `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(60_000)`, catch TimeoutError in handleKnowledgeAnalyze's existing try/catch. Re-flagged 3 runs.

title: Caption API forwards style/prompt to subprocess without allowlist or length cap
detail: api/caption.ts handleCaptionRun: `style` passed to run.py without enum check (valid: default/photography/t2i/profile/style/score/compare/review/playwright), and `prompt` has no length cap. Large prompts (up to 50MB body limit) forwarded verbatim to the VLM subprocess — DoS. style/prompt follow value-taking flags so argparse won't misparse as flags, but the lack of an allowlist/length cap is still an input-validation gap. The `image` positional is already guarded against leading-dash injection. Fix: allowlist style; cap prompt at ~4000 chars before spawning. Re-flagged 3 runs. Re-flagged this run (2026-06-23T22-35) as security-caption-64 at info severity: style follows a value-taking flag (argparse consumes it as the value, Bun.spawn argv array, no shell) so there is no RCE/injection vector; the only consequence is an out-of-set value surfaces run.py's argparse error via the generic 500 path. Marked info — garbage-in/clean-error-out, no security impact; optional hardening = validate against the documented set + return 400.

title: handleModelCheck returns raw run.py stderr to client; handleModelCheckCache is the one inconsistent handler forwarding e.message
detail: api/model-check.ts: on non-JSON output the raw decoded stderr is returned directly as the `error` field, and on a spawn exception the raw e.message is returned. This run (2026-06-20T04-15) isolated the inconsistency: every error path in this file EXCEPT handleModelCheckCache (line 67) was hardened to log server-side + return generic; handleModelCheckCache still returns `"Failed to read cache: " + (e.message || String(e))` — the one inconsistent handler, embedding filesystem paths/SQLite internals in the response. Same info-disclosure class as verify-python-leaks-stderr. Fix: align handleModelCheckCache with the others — console.error + return generic. Re-flagged 5 runs. Re-flagged this run (2026-06-21T03-54) as 2 findings (error-handling-model-check-66 + security-model-check-66) — the same handleModelCheckCache catch returning `"Failed to read cache: " + e.message`. Still open.

title: proc.stdout/stderr.getReader() runs outside the try/catch, leaving job stuck 'running'
detail: lib/subprocess.ts: proc.stdout/stderr are null-checked (line 143) inside the try/catch, but `proc.stdout.getReader()` / `proc.stderr.getReader()` on lines 210-211 run OUTSIDE that try/catch (which ends at line 133). If getReader() throws synchronously (a stream in an errored state), the exception propagates out of spawn(): finalize is never registered, the job stays status 'running' forever, the request handler crashes, and the orphaned job can never be finalized or cleanly killed. Fix: wrap the getReader() calls in the same finalize-as-failed guard used for the null-stream case (push stderr log, set status=failed, exitCode=-1, broadcastStatus, return id). Retired: single-occurrence latent trap in the subprocess class; killjob-pid-guard-and-finalize (7x, conf 0.9) is the higher-signal recurring record for this file.

title: handleListLoras/handleListVaes expose absolute filesystem paths to unauthenticated clients
detail: api/models.ts: both model-listing endpoints return `path` as an absolute filesystem path (e.g. /Users/<user>/proj/.../python/mlx-movie-director/models/lora/<name>) for every LoRA/VAE entry. The frontend only needs the model name and relative identifiers (it builds CLI args via buildCliArgs which itself resolves and validates against allowed dirs). Leaking the full absolute path reveals the OS username and directory layout of the host. Combined with the lack of auth on the API, this is an unnecessary info-disclosure vector. Fix: return the model name/relative subfolder (e.g. path: entry.name) instead of the absolute path. Re-flagged 2 runs. Retired (2026-06-23T22-35): single-operator localhost threat model bounds this to low-impact info-disclosure (OS username + dir layout); not re-flagged this run, compacts to keep active records <=40.

title: Before FLAGGING info-disclosure/error-handling/security issues, grep call-site usage + scan ~70 lines for an existing guard
detail: Mitigates the high false-positive rate at flag-time. For each candidate: (1) grep the repo for callers/readers of the flagged symbol or endpoint; (2) scan ~70 lines around the site and the auth middleware for an existing guard or benign context (localhost dev tool, functional identity, upstream try/catch). If a guard exists or the context is benign, downgrade severity or drop the finding instead of emitting a context-free pattern match. Do NOT rely on the adversarial-verify gate to filter these — it reports upheld=0 yet leaves findings verified (sample sizes are tiny: this run 1/7 upheld at 0.86 rejection, prior run 2/2 upheld — the gate is too small-sample to be a reliable filter). CALIBRATION UPDATE (2026-06-20T04-15): this run's full-scope scan produced 26 high-confidence findings with rejection_rate=0, so the close-inspection burden is lower when the finding set is already high-confidence; apply the grep+guard check most aggressively to info-disclosure/security-severity candidates where the localhost single-operator threat model downgrades real impact. UPDATE (2026-06-21T03-54): this run produced 48 findings at rejection_rate=0.31 (33 upheld) — the larger the finding set, the more BOTH upheld-and-rejected grow together; the grep+guard check remains the per-finding filter the adversarial gate cannot replace.

title: handleGetLastJob returns null when command filter is absent instead of the actual last job
detail: api/jobs.ts: the ternary's else branch is `null`, so GET /api/jobs/last without a command returns `{ job: null }` even when jobs exist. The route name implies 'most recent job regardless of command'. Latent (frontend always passes command) but any caller omitting it silently gets nothing. Fix: fall back to `jobs.find(j => j.status !== 'running') ?? null` when command is absent. Retired: single-occurrence latent trap; no caller omits command, so the dead branch never fires in practice.

title: handleGalleryImage serves any file under OUTPUT_DIRS by normalized path with no realpath or extension allowlist
detail: api/gallery.ts: containment uses path.normalize+startsWith (lexical only — no realpath), so a symlink under an output dir whose target is outside passes the check while Bun.file follows the link. No MEDIA_GLOB extension allowlist either (unlike handleGalleryDelete), so manifest.json/run.json/caption.json or attacker-placed files are servable. octet-stream+nosniff backstop prevents active execution, but sensitive companion JSON or symlinked files are readable by any local requester. Fix (two-layer): realpathSync before prefix check; gate name on MEDIA_GLOB.match like the delete path does. This run (2026-06-20T04-15) re-confirmed at info severity: the trailing-sep prefix check is CORRECT (resolvedDir = path.resolve(dir)+path.sep), the gap is purely the missing realpath — and the only actor who can plant a symlink under OUTPUT_DIRS is the operator (who already has a shell), so not exploitable by the threat model, but worth noting for defense-in-depth. Re-flagged 3 runs.

title: loadJobs crashes server boot if any persisted job has missing/non-array logs or outputUrls
detail: lib/jobstore.ts loadJobs iterates loaded jobs and reads `job.logs.length` unconditionally, then loadAndRestoreJob pushes to job.logs. If jobs.json contains a job whose `logs` (or `outputUrls`) field is undefined/null — hand-edited, partial write, older/malformed schema, or a job persisted before the LogLine migration — `job.logs.length` throws TypeError and, because loadAndRestoreJobs runs at server.ts startup, the ENTIRE server fails to boot. No defensive coercion is applied. Fix: coerce before access — `if (!Array.isArray(job.logs)) job.logs = []; if (!Array.isArray(job.outputUrls)) job.outputUrls = [];` and `if (!job.startedAt) continue;` to skip wholly malformed entries rather than crashing the migration loop.

title: saveJobs is fire-and-forget Bun.write with no serialization — concurrent overwrites lose jobs (last-completion-wins)
detail: lib/jobstore.ts saveJobs calls Bun.write(...) unawaited (.catch(()=>{})). broadcastStatus() triggers persistJobs→saveJobs on EVERY log line AND every status change. Two rapid broadcasts each snapshot and write asynchronously; the OS may complete the OLDER write after the NEWER one, clobbering newest state with a stale snapshot (last-write-wins by completion order, not issue order). On a busy job emitting many log lines this silently drops the completed/failed transition or resurrects a 'running' state from a stale write landing last. Fix: serialize with a promise chain capturing the snapshot synchronously — `let _chain = Promise.resolve(); export function saveJobs(jobs){ const snap=[...jobs]; _chain = _chain.then(()=>Bun.write(JOBS_PATH, JSON.stringify(snap,null,2)+"\n")).catch(()=>{}); return _chain; }`.

title: JobHistoryView auto-expand-most-recent-failed useState initializer runs before SWR resolves (feature is dead)
detail: Retired (2026-06-21T03-54) to compact active records to <=40 after adding higher-value type-safety records this run. ORIGINAL: frontend/views/jobs/JobHistoryView.tsx: useState(() => {...}) initializer captures `jobs` from useJobs() at first render. On first render SWR has not resolved so jobs===[], and `sorted.find(j=>j.status==='failed')` returns undefined → expandedId stays null FOREVER (the initializer never re-runs). The intended 'auto-expand the most recent failed job' UX only works if jobs are already in cache on mount; after a fresh load the feature is dead. Fix: track a loaded-once flag and expand on the transition via useEffect — `const [autoExpanded, setAutoExpanded] = useState(false); useEffect(()=>{ if(!autoExpanded && jobs.some(j=>j.status==='failed')){ const f=[...jobs].sort((a,b)=>new Date(b.startedAt)-new Date(a.startedAt)).find(j=>j.status==='failed'); if(f){ setExpandedId(f.id); setAutoExpanded(true);} } }, [jobs, autoExpanded]);`.

title: handleGallerySearch builds the FTS index with no concurrency guard — duplicate concurrent rebuilds + invalidate race
detail: api/gallery.ts handleGallerySearch: two concurrent /api/gallery/search calls both observe isIndexed()===false and each invoke buildIndex(scanAllImages()) (a filesystem scan + INSERT loop). buildIndex does `DELETE FROM images_fts` then re-inserts — if call B's DELETE lands between call A's DELETE and A's INSERTs, call A inserts into an empty table then B deletes them again, so the index ends empty/inconsistent while both think it is built. invalidateIndex() (fired on job_complete / file watcher) can flip _indexed=false mid-build too. No mutex serializes the single-writer rebuild. Fix: guard with a module-level in-flight promise — `let _buildPromise = null; export async function ensureIndex(){ if(isIndexed()) return; if(!_buildPromise) _buildPromise = (async()=>{ buildIndex(scanAllImages()); })(); await _buildPromise; _buildPromise=null; }` and have search await ensureIndex() before querying. Sibling of fts5-optimize-masks-build-failure (that is flag-ordering; this is the concurrency-guard gap). Retired: single-occurrence low-confidence; sibling fts5-optimize-masks-build-failure (4x, conf 0.9) is the higher-signal record for the gallery-index file.

title: handleRunJob response leaks the spawned child PID to the client

Low impact but unnecessary disclosure. Fix: omit pid from the client-facing response — `return Response.json({ jobId, status: job?.status });` — keep pid internal to the Job object for killJob/deleteJob use. title: useWebSocket progress regex matches incidental percentages in non-progress log lines (memory: 80%, loaded 50% of weights)
detail: frontend/hooks/ui/useWebSocket.ts line 72: `const pm = msg.line.match(/\b(\d{1,3})%/) ?? msg.line.match(/step (\d+) of (\d+)/i);`. The percent matcher `\b(\d{1,3})%` is unanchored to any progress context, so a stray number followed by '%' that is NOT actual progress (e.g. 'memory: 80%' from a system metric, or 'loaded 50% of weights at step 3 of 10' which matches 50% and ignores the more meaningful step ratio) incorrectly sets the progress bar. When the percent branch matches, pm[2] is undefined so the pct branch correctly uses +pm[1], but the SOURCE is wrong. The clamp (0..100) only bounds the value, not the relevance. Fix: restrict the percent match to an explicit progress context, e.g. `/progress[:\s]+(\d{1,3})%/i` or `/\b(\d{1,3})%\s*(?:complete|done)?/i`, and drop the bare `\b(\d{1,3})%` catch-all. Retired: single-occurrence minor UX nit (progress bar momentarily shows a wrong value); cosmetic, no recurrence.

title: knowledge-extractor formatRecord interpolates run.steps/cfg_scale/width/height/lora_scale without null guards — malformed run.json injects 'undefined' tokens into the DeepSeek prompt

The run object is guaranteed truthy by the eligible filter (requires r.run) but its SCALAR fields are NOT validated. A run.json missing steps/cfg_scale/width/height/lora_scale produces literal 'undefined' / 'undefinedxundefined' tokens in the prompt sent to DeepSeek, corrupting knowledge extraction with garbage values. run.lora_scale is also accessed directly and is undefined when no LoRA is used, producing 'none @ undefined'. Fix: default the scalars before interpolating — `const steps = run.steps ?? "?"; const cfg = run.cfg_scale ?? "?"; const size = run.width && run.height ? \`${run.width}x${run.height}\` : "?"; const loraScale = run.lora_scale ?? "none";` — so malformed run.json degrades gracefully instead of injecting 'undefined'. title: useJobs (and other useWebSocketEvents consumers) revalidate on a WS message type the server never broadcasts — stale list for up to the refreshInterval
detail: frontend/hooks/queries/useJobs.ts: the useWebSocketEvents callback calls mutate() on `msg.type === "job_complete" || "job_failed" || "job_start"` for an instant jobs-list refresh. But the server NEVER broadcasts `type: "job_start"` — every broadcast site (api/ws.ts onStatus emits only job_complete/job_failed/log; server.ts and api/bundle.ts emit only hmr-reload/gallery-updated/hmr-error; onLog emits only log) has no code path producing it. So when a new job is spawned via /api/run, /api/replay, /api/selftest, or /api/model-check/scan, the jobs list does NOT refresh immediately — it updates only on the next refreshInterval tick (5s) or the eventual complete/failed. The History view (and any useJobs consumer) shows stale data for up to 5s after starting a job. Symptom is limited to the just-started window (complete/failed are emitted), hence medium not high. Two fix paths: (a) emit a distinct start signal — add `this.broadcastStatus(job)` in lib/subprocess.ts spawn() after `this.jobs.set(id, job)` and have ws.ts onStatus emit `{ type: "job_status", job }` for running too, with useJobs revalidating on it; or (b) simpler frontend-only fix — also refresh on the shared `log` message when a brand-new jobId appears. Class lesson: WS-revalidate hooks must only listen for types the server actually emits — grep the broadcast sites (ws.ts onStatus/onLog) before adding a type to the match list.

title: buildCliArgs forwards select/multiselect values to run.py without validating against field.choices (defense-in-depth gap)
detail: lib/args.ts buildCliArgs handles `select` (line 45) and `multiselect` (line 49) by trimming and pushing the raw value as `--flag value` — neither branch validates against the schema's field.choices allowlist (grep confirms no choices check in args.ts). So a POST /api/run body with an off-menu pipeline/lora value passes validateParams (required-fields only) and arrives at run.py as `--pipeline <value>`. THREAT MODEL CAVEAT: localhost single-operator, and argparse binds a leading-dash value after a value-taking flag as that flag's VALUE (not a new flag — distinct from positional argv injection), so this cannot inject a NEW flag; the realistic impact is run.py executing a model/pipeline string the GUI never intended to offer, not RCE. Still, the UI guarantees a fixed option set and the backend silently accepts anything — defense-in-depth is missing. Fix: in the select branch, when field.choices is defined (skip choicesFrom whose options are dynamic), `if (field.choices && !field.choices.some(c => c.value === value.trim())) throw new Error('Invalid value for ${key}')`; validate every multiselect item similarly. Distinct from args-subprocess-no-containment (path fields) and caption-style-no-enum-validation (caption style). Retired: single-occurrence low-confidence; localhost threat model + value-taking-flag semantics bound the impact to defense-in-depth only.

title: api/knowledge.ts module-scoped _scanCache is shared across requests; generateMissingCaptions mutates record objects in place (latent race)
detail: api/knowledge.ts: _scanCache is a module-level mutable read by handleKnowledgeCaptionMissing and handleKnowledgeAnalyze (`const records = _scanCache ?? scanOutputDirs()`). Two concurrent requests race on this shared state: handleKnowledgeCaptionMissing sets `_scanCache = null` at line 41 after caption generation while a concurrent analyze holds the same array reference, and generateMissingCaptions mutates `rec.caption`/`rec.hasCaption` IN PLACE on the shared record objects. Single-thread JS mitigates the worst races, but the in-place mutation + non-atomic cache reassignment is a latent correctness hazard: an analyze running concurrently with a caption-missing run can operate on a records array whose caption fields are mid-mutation. Fix: pass records by value (snapshot the array + shallow-copy records before the caption loop so a concurrent analyze reads a consistent view), or have generateMissingCaptions return updated copies rather than mutating shared objects. Retired: single-occurrence low-confidence latent trap; single-thread JS bounds the practical impact.

title: DNS-rebinding bypass of the origin allowlist is a FALSE POSITIVE under the browser-forbidden-header threat model — Origin/Host are attacker-unforgeable
detail: Counter-analysis to csrf-host-header-rebinding (7x active): the committed-KB 'DNS-rebinding bypass' framing is a false positive against a cross-SITE attacker. Origin and Host are browser-forbidden headers (the Fetch standard forbids JS from setting them on a request), so a malicious page at https://evil.com CANNOT produce `Origin: http://127.0.0.1:<port>` — the browser stamps Origin with the embedding page's own origin, which fails the loopback [127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1]] allowlist. A genuine DNS-rebinding attack sets Host/Origin to the ATTACKER's domain (the resolved IP), not to 127.0.0.1, so it too fails the allowlist. The origin-allowlist construction (now consolidated in lib/origin.ts originAllowed as of 2026-06-21T03-54) is therefore SOUND against the cross-site/cross-origin threat the framing worried about. CAVEAT: this does NOT clear csrf-host-header-rebinding entirely — the underlying concern worth keeping is the DRY-duplication (now fixed) and defense-in-depth (a fixed Set literal is cleaner than Host-derived port extraction). LESSON: when a security finding's exploit path depends on a browser-forbidden header, downgrade it — the local single-operator + browser-forbidden-Origin model makes the loopback allowlist sufficient; spend review effort on the actually-exploitable classes (validate-python-path-substring-not-prefix RCE, path-prefix-missing-separator).

title: searchImages() early-returns [] when toFtsQuery() yields empty, dropping the LIKE filename fallback for punctuation-only queries
detail: lib/gallery-index.ts searchImages: `const ftsQuery = toFtsQuery(q); if (!ftsQuery) return [];` bails before the LIKE filename branch. toFtsQuery strips ['"()^*] and returns "" when the remaining tokens are empty, so a query ENTIRELY made of stripped chars (e.g. `"()"`, `"***"`, or any punctuation-only input) yields ftsQuery="" and the function returns [] WITHOUT running the LIKE filename search that would have matched such a literal string against filenames. The early-return conflates 'no meaningful FTS tokens' with 'no search at all', dropping the substring path. Reachable: api/gallery.ts handleGallerySearch only guards `if (!q)` (empty string), so any non-empty punctuation-only `q` flows straight into searchImages and silently returns nothing. This is the SAME gallery-index.ts locus as fts5-optimize-masks-build-failure (build-time flag ordering) but a DISTINCT bug — this is the QUERY-time fallback logic. Fix: do not bail on empty ftsQuery; compute likeRows unconditionally (it builds likePattern from q), only run the FTS sub-query when ftsQuery is non-empty (`const ftsRows = ftsQuery ? db.query(...).all(ftsQuery, ...) : []`), keep the LIKE search always, and return [] only if BOTH ftsRows and likeRows are empty. GENERAL PATTERN: when a search fn chains a full-text-index query with a substring/LIKE fallback, never gate the WHOLE fn on the FTS-normalized query being non-empty — gate each sub-query independently so the substring path survives punctuation-only inputs that the FTS tokenizer strips to nothing.

title: CommandPalette Recent-Jobs rows are highlightable + visible but non-functional via BOTH keyboard (Enter no-op) and mouse (onClick only closes)
detail: Retired (2026-06-21T03-54) to compact active records to <=40 after adding 4 new high-value lever/type-safety records this run. ORIGINAL: frontend/components/CommandPalette.tsx handleKeyDown Enter branch only acts when `highlighted < filtered.length` — it only opens command items. Items at index >= filtered.length are the 'Recent Jobs' entries appended below the command list (idx = filtered.length + i). Arrow navigation bounds `highlighted` to totalItems-1 (which INCLUDES recent jobs), so the user can highlight a recent job, but pressing Enter is a no-op for it. Worse, the onClick for recent-job rows is `() => onClose()` — it closes the palette WITHOUT navigating to the job at all. So the entire recent-jobs feature (highlightable, visible, counted in totalItems = filtered.length + (query ? 0 : recentJobs.length)) is non-functional via both inputs. The index math is right; no handler consumes the job index. GENERAL PATTERN: when a list appends a secondary category below the primary filtered set and reuses a single highlighted cursor across BOTH, the Enter handler must branch on the index boundary (`if highlighted < filtered.length {...primary} else {...secondary}`) — and every rendered row's onClick must dispatch the same action its highlight-Enter would, not just dismiss. Fix: in the Enter branch, when highlighted >= filtered.length compute `recentJobs[highlighted - filtered.length]` and onSelect({type:'job', action: job.id}) before onClose(); and in the row onClick replace `() => onClose()` with a handler that actually navigates.

title: CommandForm has a dead `if (field.type === "toggle")` branch inside the full-width single-field block — unreachable because toggle is never full-width
detail: frontend/components/CommandForm.tsx: isFullWidth() returns true only for types prompt/image/images/loras — toggle is NOT in that set. The single-field branch computes `const single = row.length === 1 && isFullWidth(row[0])`, so when `single` is true, row[0].type can NEVER be 'toggle'. The inner `if (field.type === "toggle")` inside that block is therefore dead code that can never execute; the intended toggle-row layout is handled by the separate `row.every((f) => f.type === "toggle")` block lower down. Not a runtime crash, but misleading dead logic that suggests a code path that never runs — a maintenance trap if someone later adds 'toggle' to isFullWidth expecting this branch to cover it (it would silently do nothing because the dedicated toggle-row branch below already consumed those rows). GENERAL PATTERN: when a dispatch branches on a TYPE/property that a guard further up already excluded, the inner branch is dead — verify the branch is reachable by checking the upstream guard's input set, not just that the code compiles. Fix: delete the dead `if (field.type === "toggle")` block inside the single branch; single-field toggles are already covered by the general toggle-row branch (or the final form-row fallback).

title: handleClearJobs has an unreachable `if (req.method !== "DELETE")` 405 guard — the router only dispatches it on DELETE, so the branch is dead
detail: api/jobs.ts handleClearJobs opens with `if (req.method !== "DELETE") return Response.json({ok:false,error:"Method not allowed"},{status:405})`, but api/routes.ts only routes this handler when `pathname === "/api/jobs/all" && method === "DELETE"`. The check can NEVER be true so the 405 branch is dead code — a misleading defense-in-depth guard that implies the handler can be reached with other methods (it cannot via the central router). Not a runtime bug, but the same unreachable-defense pattern as commandform-dead-toggle-in-fullwidth-branch. NOTE the sibling handleGalleryDelete (gallery.ts) has the same dead per-handler method-guard shape; handleClearJobs is the only one of the DELETE routes carrying the redundant branch. Fix: remove the per-handler method check (the router guarantees DELETE). If defense-in-depth is genuinely desired, centralize it in handleApi rather than scattering dead 405 branches per handler. NOTE (2026-06-21T03-54): handleApi was refactored to a route table this run (STATIC_ROUTES + PREFIX_ROUTES), making the central-dispatch guarantee even stronger — the per-handler dead 405 is now doubly redundant. GENERAL PATTERN: when a central router already dispatches on method+pathname, a per-handler re-check of the same method is dead code — either trust the router or centralize the check once, do not duplicate unreachable guards that mislead future readers into thinking the handler has a wider entry surface than it does.

title: wsClient singleton's addListener cleanup never closes the WebSocket when the last handler unsubscribes — idle socket leaks for the SPA lifetime
detail: Retired (2026-06-21T03-54) to compact active records to <=40; minor single-socket idle leak, lower-signal than ws-reconnect-timer-not-cleared (4x) which covers the same wsClient singleton. ORIGINAL: frontend/hooks/ui/wsClient.ts: the cleanup returned by addListener (the `return () => { _handlers.delete(handler); }`) only removes the handler from the set; it never closes `_ws`. When all subscribers unregister the WebSocket stays open until page unload — a dangling-singleton resource leak, exactly the kind the module-top comment claims to manage. The onclose handler (line 26) already gates reconnect on `_handlers.size > 0`, so it will not needlessly reconnect, but the IDLE socket is leaked for the rest of the SPA lifetime. With many view mount/unmount cycles this is a minor leak (one socket), not a correctness bug. This is a DISTINCT facet of the same wsClient.ts singleton flagged by ws-reconnect-timer-not-cleared (that is the reconnect double-fire; this is the never-close-on-last-unsubscribe) — two separate lifecycle bugs in the one shared broadcast socket that drives ALL listeners (useJobs revalidation, gallery-updated, hmr-reload). Fix: in the cleanup, after deleting, if the set is now empty close the socket — `if (_handlers.size === 0 && _ws) { _ws.onclose = null; _ws.close(); _ws = null; }`. GENERAL PATTERN: a subscribe/unsubscribe singleton that opens a resource on first-subscribe must symmetrically CLOSE it on last-unsubscribe; a cleanup that only mutates the handler set without checking for the empty-set transition leaks the underlying resource. Reinforces fix-not-ported-to-sibling-sites (the wsClient singleton keeps accumulating lifecycle bugs because fixes land on useWebSocket.ts not here).

title: parseCaptionField reads legacy flat `.caption` key, so current multi-style `.styles.review.caption` files parse as undefined → every new T2I record silently excluded from DeepSeek learning
detail: lib/knowledge-extractor.ts scanOutputDirs reads a .caption.json and calls `parseCaptionField(captionRaw.caption)`, assuming the OLD flat format where the scores object lives at top-level `.caption`. But the CURRENT on-disk format (captionFormat.ts) is `{ image, model, updated_style, styles: { [style]: { model, elapsed_sec, caption: <scores> } } }`. For any caption produced by the current `run.py caption --style review`, `captionRaw.caption` is `undefined` (scores live at `captionRaw.styles.review.caption`), so `parseCaptionField(undefined)` returns null → hasCaption=false, qualityScore=null. Consequence: every newly-captioned T2I record is treated as uncaptioned and silently excluded from DeepSeek analysis (the `eligible` filter requires r.caption) — the knowledge pipeline NEVER learns from the current caption format. The SAME bug is duplicated in generateMissingCaptions (it re-reads the freshly-generated caption and fails to parse it the same way, so the in-memory rec stays hasCaption=false). The gallery READ path (gallery.ts) avoids this via normalizeCaptionFile + pickCaptionStyle, proving the knowledge reader should reuse the same shared normalizer rather than re-deriving the field path. Fix (both sites): `const norm = normalizeCaptionFile(captionRaw); const entry = pickCaptionStyle(norm, 'review') ?? pickCaptionStyle(norm, norm?.updated_style ?? 'default'); const caption = entry ? parseCaptionField(entry.caption) : null;` — falls back across styles so both legacy flat and current multi-style files parse. CONFIRMED + NARROWED TO EXACT LOCI (2026-06-21T02-19, run 2026-06-21T02-19-16): this run re-flagged the SAME root cause as two high-severity correctness findings, pinning the exact lines — knowledge-extractor.ts scanOutputDirs line 84 (`parseCaptionField(captionRaw.caption)` on the initial scan) AND generateMissingCaptions line 193 (the post-caption RE-READ `parseCaptionField(captionRaw.caption)`). Both adversarially UPHELD. The line-193 site is the more damaging: after generateMissingCaptions successfully writes a fresh review caption and re-reads it, `captionRaw.caption` is STILL undefined (the writer wraps it in styles.review.caption), so rec.hasCaption stays false, rec.qualityScore stays null, the 'Captions' tab missing-count never decreases, AND the record is re-queued for captioning forever (infinite re-caption loop burning GPU). Net effect confirmed: the entire knowledge pipeline ingests ZERO modern output. NOTE (2026-06-21T03-54): this run's fixes to knowledge-extractor.ts (DeepSeek response interface + cfg cast drop) did NOT touch the caption-format-drift at lines 84/193 — this highest-value defect is STILL OPEN across 3 runs now; it needs its own fix-mode pass landing the normalize+pickCaptionStyle change. GENERAL PATTERN: when a reader derives a field path from an on-disk JSON format that has since gained a versioned/wrapper layer (here a per-style map), the reader silently returns null instead of throwing — there is no error, the pipeline just stops ingesting; always reuse the writer's own normalizer rather than re-deriving the path, and add a smoke test that asserts a freshly-written record round-trips through the reader.

title: Extracting a duplicated guard/expression into a single shared helper PERMANENTLY closes the whole fix-not-ported-to-sibling-sites recurrence class
detail: When the same logic is copy-pasted across N files (CORS allowlist in routes.ts+ws.ts; containment checks across paths/caption/gallery; reconnect-timer clear in useWebSocket+wsClient), re-flagging the unfixed sibling run after run is the dominant review-loop tax. FIX APPLIED 2026-06-21T03-54 (effort:medium+fix:true) on the CORS-allowlist duplication: created lib/origin.ts with `originAllowed(origin, host): boolean` (LOOPBACK_HOSTS const + port-from-Host regex + DEFAULT_PORT=3099 in ONE place), routes.ts and ws.ts both import + call it. This structurally ELIMINATES the cross-origin-allowlist-duplication recurrence — there is now only one site to fix. The two prior distinct 403 response bodies were preserved by checking !host after originAllowed returns false (originAllowed encodes 'absent Origin -> allow, absent host -> deny'). LESSON (load-bearing): the 'extract shared helper' refactor is strictly stronger than the 'grep-port the fix to siblings' rule (fix-not-ported-to-sibling-sites) — grep-porting depends on a human remembering every sibling each time; extraction makes the single-source-of-truth structurally enforced by the compiler/import graph. PREFERENCE ORDER for a recurring duplication-driven finding: (1) extract a shared helper and call it from all sites (permanent); (2) grep-port the fix to siblings (manual, recurrence-prone); (3) leave duplicated (re-flagged forever). Same lever applies to containment-check-reimplemented (4 sites) and the WS reconnect-timer (2 sites) — both are extract-helper candidates. Verified safe: 574/0 tests, tscDelta=0, no regressions. NEW DUPLICATION INSTANCES this run (2026-06-23T22-35) all confirm the lever: (a) QUANT_SUFFIX_RE + normalizeTransformerKey duplicated byte-identical between api/abTest.ts and frontend/utils/galleryGroup.ts (quant-suffix detection would drift on a new suffix like nf4); (b) /output/<N>/<file> URL parse+dirIdx-bounds+path.join copy-pasted 3x (caption.ts x2, abTest.ts resolveGalleryUrl x1); (c) subprocess stdout/stderr concurrent-drain pattern (new Response(stream).text() before await proc.exited) repeated verbatim in 4 files with the same ~64KB pipe-buffer comment; (d) loopback host allowlist [localhost,127.0.0.1,::1] hardcoded in api/config.ts AND api/vlm.ts AND lib/origin.ts (3 copies, two bare '::1' vs one bracketed) — origin.ts was created to be the single source but config.ts/vlm.ts did not adopt it; (e) VLM model id constants (PREFERRED_VLM/DEFAULT_VLM) hardcoded in api/vlm.ts with a 'mirror caption.py manually' comment (drift hazard, no sync test); (f) stderr truncation magic number 300/200 scattered across gallery/abTest/knowledge-extractor. All are extract-helper candidates: promote resolveGalleryUrl→shared lib/paths.resolveOutputUrl, spawnCapture→shared lib/subprocess.captureSpawn, quant regex→shared module, adopt origin.ts LOOPBACK_HOSTS in config.ts+vlm.ts.

title: Replace a long if/else method+pathname dispatch chain with a declarative STATIC_ROUTES + PREFIX_ROUTES table — static-first matching is load-bearing
detail: FIX APPLIED 2026-06-21T03-54 on api/routes.ts handleApi (was a ~170-line, 25+ branch if/else chain — routes-handler-ifelse-chain): built STATIC_ROUTES (exact pathname+method) and PREFIX_ROUTES (startsWith dynamic-id, e.g. /api/jobs/<id>) at module scope, handleApi now loops STATIC_ROUTES first then PREFIX_ROUTES. The static-first ordering is LOAD-BEARING and was documented in the new code: /api/jobs/last (GET) and /api/jobs/all (DELETE) are STATIC entries that MUST win over the /api/jobs/ PREFIX route, so matching static-first prevents those literal paths from being mis-read as job ids. Adding a new endpoint is now a one-line table entry instead of inserting into the chain. The CSRF/origin guard stays at the top of handleApi (single entry point preserved); all handler signatures + response shapes byte-for-byte equivalent. LESSON: a declarative route table turns 'ordering-dependent implicit dispatch' into 'ordering-explicit array position' — the prefix-shadowing hazard becomes a visible, reviewable property of the table rather than an emergent property of the chain. Verified safe: 574/0 tests, tscDelta=0. Reusable for any central-dispatch function that grows past ~10 branches; pair with the 'drop dead per-handler method guards' cleanup (clearjobs-unreachable-method-guard) since the table makes the central-dispatch guarantee explicit.

title: `as any` / untyped JSON.parse at HTTP+JSON boundaries is the reusable type-safety check — define an interface or runtime-narrow at each
detail: REUSABLE CHECK: grep for `as any` and bare `JSON.parse(...)` (no `as <Type>` and no runtime narrowing) across api/ + lib/; each hit is a candidate finding. This run (2026-06-21T03-54) the type-safety dimension became the LARGEST finding bucket (13 of 48) — all concrete `as any` / untyped-parse loci: ws.ts `JSON.parse(msg)` → subscribedJobId:string with no narrowing; knowledge-extractor DeepSeek `res.json() as any` then `data.choices?.[0]?.message?.content`; knowledge-extractor `(cfg as any).deepseekApiKey` (AppConfig ALREADY declares it optional — pure papered-over cast); vlm.ts `/models` `let data: any`; gallery-index buildIndex/searchImages/extract* all `any[]` despite a concrete ImageEntry type existing; frontend WsMessage loose `type: string` instead of a discriminated union; bundle `(l as any).position`; model-check `JSON.parse(stdout)` untyped; selftest `variants: any[]`; models manifest JSON untyped; jobstore migration `as any` casts. 3 were FIXED this run (ws.ts narrowing `as {type?:string; jobId?:unknown}` + `typeof jobId==='string'`; DeepSeek response `as DeepSeekChatResponse`; dropped cfg cast). GENERAL PATTERNS at these boundaries: (a) `(cfg as any).x` when the interface already declares x — drop the cast, the optional typing flows for free (see cfg-as-any-bypasses-declared-optional); (b) `JSON.parse(x)` consumed by a typed downstream — narrow with `as <Shape>` AND a runtime guard on the discriminating field before forwarding; (c) a loose `type: string` interface over a known finite message set — convert to a discriminated union for exhaustiveness. The adversarial gate upheld type-safety findings at a high rate (they are concrete loci with unambiguous fixes), making this the highest-fix-yield dimension.

title: `(cfg as any).x` when AppConfig already declares `x?` is a papered-over cast that hides the real optional typing — drop the cast
detail: lib/knowledge-extractor.ts accessed DeepSeek config via `(cfg as any).deepseekApiKey ?? process.env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` and `(cfg as any).deepseekModel ?? 'deepseek-chat'`, but lib/config.ts AppConfig (lines 17-18) ALREADY declares both `deepseekApiKey?: string` and `deepseekModel?: string`. The cast bypasses the declared optional typing, so a refactor renaming the field would be a silent runtime break instead of a compile-time error — exactly the 'unsafe type assertion that should be a real property access' pattern. FIX APPLIED 2026-06-21T03-54: dropped the casts to `cfg.deepseekApiKey ?? process.env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` and `cfg.deepseekModel ?? 'deepseek-chat'`; the real optional typing now flows to the compiler. GENERAL PATTERN: before writing `(X as any).prop`, grep the interface/type declaration for `prop` — if it is already declared (even optional), the cast is pure harm (hides typing, blocks rename-refactor safety); access it directly. The cast is only defensible when the field genuinely is not on any declared type (e.g. an undocumented runtime addition like Bun's BuildMessage.position — there, declare an extension interface instead, see bundle `(l as any).position` variant). Reinforces type-safety-any-boundary.

title: NumberField `onChange={(v) => setField(key, v || null)}` silently drops a legitimate 0 to null (treats 0 as 'no value')
detail: frontend/views/workflow/VideoT2i2vView.tsx: the CFG Scale / T2I Seed Override / STG Scale / stage-steps NumberFields bind `onChange={(v) => setField("cfg_scale", v || null)}` etc. The `v || null` falsy-coalesces: when the user types 0 (a valid t2i_seed override, and 0 is in the valid range for several distilled-model params), `0 || null` evaluates to `null`, so the field is treated as 'no override' and the legitimate 0 is silently discarded. The downstream `if (state.cfg_scale != null)` guard then forwards null (not 0). For seed this is the worst: a t2i_seed of 0 — a real, common override — becomes null (treated as 'no override'), so the T2I stage runs with the default seed instead of 0. GENERAL PATTERN: never use `x || default` to coalesce a numeric field where 0 is a valid value — use an explicit undefined/null check (`v === undefined ? null : v`) so 0 survives. The mirror anti-pattern is the argparse-sentinel rule on the Python side (default=None to detect flag-override, never magic-number-compare vs a concrete default). Same root: falsy-coalescing conflates 'absent' with 'zero'. Code-quality-VideoT2i2vView-57 (magic-number defaults repeated in FALLBACK_DEFAULTS + inline ?? fallbacks) is a sibling code-quality nit in the same file.

title: Degenerate ternary `cond ? X : X` where both arms return the identical value — dead logic that obscures intent and hides a missing branch
detail: api/abTest.ts buildRegenCommand: `const sub = pipeline === "zimage" ? "t2i" : "t2i";` — both arms yield the identical string 't2i'. This is a no-op ternary: a reader assumes the branches differ (why test pipeline at all?), and a future non-zimage pipeline that SHOULD map to a different subcommand (e.g. 'i2i') would silently stay broken because the second arm was never corrected. GENERAL PATTERN: a conditional whose both branches are identical is either (a) a typo where the second arm was meant to differ, or (b) a leftover from a refactor that removed the differentiation — either way it is dead logic. Reusable check: grep for `\?.*:.*:` ternaries where the two arm-expressions are byte-equal (or trivially equal after whitespace); each hit is either a bug or dead code to collapse to a bare assignment (`const sub = "t2i";`). Sibling code-quality nits this run (abTest-309 hardcoded python path in the same regen string, abTest-429 metric-direction sets hardcoded inline) reinforce that buildRegenCommand is a recurring code-quality locus.

title: handleDeleteImage: on partial-failure (data.ok=false, SOME companions failed but the main image was unlinked) the gallery is never refreshed, leaving a stale card for a now-deleted file
detail: frontend/views/gallery/GalleryView.tsx handleDeleteImage branches `if (data.ok)` for success (setAllImages filter + setRefreshKey) and `else` for failure (toast only). The server returns `ok: failed.length === 0` (api/gallery.ts), so when SOME companion files fail to delete but the MAIN image succeeded, data.ok is false and the else branch runs — it shows a toast but never calls setRefreshKey/setAllImages. The main image was already unlinked server-side, so its card stays visible (stale) until the next WS-triggered refresh. The bug is specifically the partial-success case: main file gone, card remains. GENERAL PATTERN: a UI optimistic/sync handler that branches on an aggregate success flag (ok === all-succeeded) must still refresh state when the PRIMARY operation succeeded even if SECONDARY/companion operations failed — the aggregate flag conflates 'main op failed' with 'main op ok but a companion failed'. Fix: in the else branch still refresh (`setRefreshKey((k)=>k+1)` after the toast), or change the condition to refresh whenever data.deleted?.length is non-empty. Sibling of gallery-delete-misses-multi-segment-companions (4x, the server-side companion-asymmetry facet) — this is the client-side stale-card facet of the same delete path.
